editions.headline: Golden Knights steal Game 1 in Denver
editions.summary: A quiet night on the schedule — just one game — but a loud result: Vegas opened the Western Conference Final with a 4-2 road win over Colorado behind a 36-save night from Carter Hart. The Eastern Conference Final opens tonight in Raleigh, with red-hot Carolina (8-0 this postseason) hosting the upstart Canadiens.

games.context: Western Conference Final · Game 1 · Ball Arena, Denver
games.detail: Carter Hart made 36 saves. Dylan Coghlan (first career playoff goal), Pavel Dorofeyev (PPG, NHL-leading 10th playoff goal), Brett Howden and Nic Dowd (empty-netter) scored for Vegas. Valeri Nichushkin and Gabriel Landeskog replied for Colorado, which played without Cale Makar (undisclosed injury). Scott Wedgewood stopped 24.

vgk.series: Lead the Colorado Avalanche 1-0 in the Western Conference Final
vgk.spotlight: Vegas players hold the top spot in playoff points (Marner, 18), goals (Dorofeyev, 10) and assists (Eichel, 14). Few teams have ever driven the scoring race this thoroughly this deep into a run — and in Game 1 the depth showed too, with Dylan Coghlan and Nic Dowd chipping in behind a 36-save wall from Carter Hart.
notes: Carter Hart was the difference in Game 1, turning aside 36 of 38 shots in a hostile Ball Arena.
Pavel Dorofeyev scored his NHL-leading 10th goal of the playoffs — the 5th player in franchise history with a double-digit goal total in a single postseason.
Brett Howden extended his road goal streak to six games (7 goals) and notched his 3rd game-winner, tying the franchise single-postseason record.
Dylan Coghlan scored his first career playoff goal — and his first NHL goal since Dec. 17, 2021.
Mark Stone missed his fourth straight game with a lower-body injury after taking a morning skate.

podcast_angles: The 8-0 Hurricanes: is Carolina's historic start sustainable, or is a well-rested team about to get tested by a Montreal club that's in rhythm? Game 1 tonight tells us a lot.
Vegas's scoring monopoly — Marner, Dorofeyev and Eichel hold the NHL lead in playoff points, goals and assists. When has one team ever owned the scoring race this thoroughly this deep?
Carter Hart's redemption arc: 36 saves in a hostile Game 1. Frame what his playoff form means for the Golden Knights' Cup window.
The youth movement: Montreal is the youngest conference finalist in 33 years, echoing the Cup-winning 1993 Canadiens. Lessons of young teams that go deep.
Cale Makar's mystery injury — how much does it swing the Western Final, and how should Colorado adjust if he misses Game 2?

editions.headline: Canadiens Shock the 'Canes With Four-Goal First
editions.summary: The Montreal Canadiens detonated on Carolina in Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Final, scoring four times in the opening period en route to a stunning 6-2 road victory at Lenovo Center. Juraj Slafkovsky (2G, 1A), Nick Suzuki (3A), Cole Caufield (1G, 1A), and Jakob Dobes (24 saves) starred as Montreal handed the previously unbeaten Hurricanes their first loss of the 2026 playoffs. Meanwhile the Western Conference Final resumes tonight in Denver, with Vegas looking to go up 2-0 on Colorado after Game 1's 4-2 road win.

games.context: Eastern Conference Final · Game 1 · Lenovo Center, Raleigh, NC
games.detail: Montreal pounced for four first-period goals on a Carolina team that had been idle for 11+ days. Cole Caufield and Phillip Danault scored in the opening four minutes, Alexandre Texier added a third, and Ivan Demidov finished a breakaway to shock the Hurricanes 4-1 by the midway point of the first. Juraj Slafkovsky added two third-period goals — his second an empty-netter — to complete the route. Nick Suzuki totaled three assists. Jakob Dobes stopped 24 shots for Montreal. For Carolina — 11-0 entering this series — it was a jarring first loss of the 2026 postseason.

podcast_angles: The Canadiens are for real — four first-period goals on the league's best team in the East. Is this the real Montreal or were the Hurricanes just rusty after 11+ days off?
Carolina went 11-0 before Game 1 — is this the normal volatility of a long layoff, or did Montreal expose a structural weakness the rest of the hockey world should pay attention to?
VGK's monopoly on the scoring race: Marner (pts), Dorofeyev (goals), Eichel (assists) — all from the same club. How rare is that, and what does it tell you about their Cup odds?
The forfeited 2026 second-round pick: what does losing that asset mean for Vegas's roster-building window if they win — or lose — the Cup this year?
Game 2 preview tonight: with Stone still out, McNabb back from suspension, and Makar's status murky for Colorado — what's the biggest factor in deciding who takes a 2-0 series lead?

rumors.content: The NHL denied the Golden Knights' appeal of their sanctions. The $100,000 fine to head coach John Tortorella and the forfeiture of Vegas's 2026 second-round draft pick are both upheld. Friedman noted there is a possibility that future compliance could be considered, but the draft penalty is not expected to be reversed.
The NHL has informed teams that the salary cap for 2026-27 will reach an all-time high of $104 million, giving active clubs significant flexibility in free agency this summer.

Toronto's new GM John Chayka is essentially open to listening to offers on any Maple Leafs player except team captain Auston Matthews. Players like Nylander and Rielly hold no-movement clauses. This does not signal a fire sale — Chayka is retooling, not rebuilding, and asking prices will be high.

Dreger reached out to former NHL head coach Mike Babcock about speculation linking him to the Edmonton Oilers. Babcock's response: "Dregs, I'm retired. Loving it." The Oilers coaching search continues.

Seravalli noted that the VGK sanctions robbed the team of positive media coverage entering the WCF. Instead of the story being Vegas's impressive playoff run, the pre-series narrative centered on the Torts fine and the forfeited pick — putting the coaching staff and front office on the defensive.

injuries.name: Mark Stone
injuries.detail: Stone has missed five consecutive games since leaving Game 3 of R2 vs. Anaheim in late May. No official return timeline. Practiced lightly but remains day-to-day heading into WCF Game 2.

injuries.name: William Karlsson
injuries.detail: Karlsson has been out since Nov. 8, 2025, and has not played in the 2026 playoffs. His availability, if any, would only come in the deep rounds.

injuries.name: Cale Makar
injuries.detail: Makar did not play in WCF Game 1 and his status for Game 2 tonight remains unclear. A major factor in the series — his absence was notable in Colorado's 4-2 loss.

news.headline: Canadiens score 4 in 1st period, shock previously unbeaten Hurricanes 6-2 in ECF Game 1
news.detail: Montreal became just the 3rd team since 2010 to score four or more goals in the first period of a conference final game. Carolina, which had swept Ottawa and Philadelphia without breaking a sweat, looked flat and ill-prepared for the speed of the Canadiens. Game 2 is Saturday night in Raleigh.

news.headline: NHL denies Golden Knights sanctions appeal — $100K fine and 2026 second-round pick forfeiture stand
news.detail: The NHL upheld its penalties against the Vegas Golden Knights stemming from repeated violations of playoff media access rules. Head coach John Tortorella was fined $100,000 and the team forfeits its 2026 second-round draft pick. The appeal was heard in New York on May 20.

news.headline: 2026-27 NHL salary cap to reach $104 million — Friedman
news.detail: Per Elliotte Friedman, the NHL has informed teams the cap ceiling for next season will be $104 million, an all-time high. This gives teams across the league significant flexibility in shaping their rosters for the future.

news.headline: Maple Leafs GM Chayka listening to offers on all players except Auston Matthews
news.detail: New Toronto general manager John Chayka, hired May 3, is signaling a major retool. Sources say he is open to discussing any player except captain Auston Matthews. Some players (Nylander, Rielly) have NMCs. Chayka is expected to set high asking prices rather than stage a fire sale.

news.headline: Cale Makar's status unclear heading into WCF Game 2 tonight
news.detail: Colorado Avalanche defenseman Cale Makar missed WCF Game 1 with an undisclosed injury and has not been confirmed for tonight's Game 2 in Denver. His absence would be significant for a Colorado team that needs to even the series.
